nationalMeanPerCandidate2010USD.source: Ballotpedia, 'State-by-state comparison of donations to state house/senate campaigns' (FollowTheMoney/NIMSP data, 2010 cycle); mean = total contributions / candidates

nationalMedianEstimateUSD.derivation: 2010 means x CPI ~1.44, then median ~= 40% of mean (candidate receipts are right-skewed); cross-checked with Wisconsin 2024 medians (~$10k assembly, ~$60k senate by July 1, Marquette Law blog) and Pennsylvania 2023 first-time winners ($128k house, $496k senate)

byStateMeanPerCandidate2010.note: Mean (not median) receipts per candidate in 2010, nominal dollars; multiply by ~1.44 for 2025 dollars (estimate). 10 largest and 10 smallest states by population; full 48-state set in allStates2010.
byStateMeanPerCandidate2010.source: Ballotpedia, 'State-by-state comparison of donations to state house/senate campaigns' (FollowTheMoney/NIMSP data, 2010 cycle); mean = total contributions / candidates

recentIncumbentAverages2022.source: Ballotpedia campaign finance analysis of contested 2022 general elections (incumbents)

mayor.source: Estimate: no national study by city size found; bands set from local reporting (e.g. Missoula mayoral poll alone $15-25k, Montana COPP; NYC council public-finance data, Brennan Center) and city campaign finance portals

cityCouncil.source: Estimate as above; NYC council median publicly financed candidate (Brennan Center); 61 California cities study (California Journal of Politics and Policy) found few credible council campaigns without money even in small cities

countyCommission.source: Estimate from local reports: Albany County WY 2022 five candidates raised ~$41k total; Cumberland County NC 2024 six candidates $183k in 6 months; Johnson County KS 2018 most candidates >$15k; Columbia County GA 2026 chair $180k vs $8.7k

broadcastTvCPM.source: AdWave, 'Political Ad Rates 2026' and 'Political Advertising Costs: What Campaigns Should Budget in 2026' (vendor); local linear $15-35 CPM, effective CPM against registered voters in a district $30-100+
broadcastTvCPM.note: Political rates rise sharply in the final 60 days (lowest-unit-charge applies to candidates only); vendor source

yardSign.source: Retail listings (Walmart, Etsy, Tampa Printing, SignMission) for 18x24 coroplast with H-stake; bulk 250-1,000 run price is an estimate from printer price lists

poll.source: High Plains Public Radio 2024-10-14 (Texas pollster: ~$100 per completed phone interview, internet about half); Daily Montanan 2023-08-22 (experts: local poll $15k-$25k on the low end)

paidCanvasserHourly.source: 2024 job postings: Antelope Valley CA $18; Virginia Beach $22; Denver, Salt Lake City, New York $25; San Francisco $25-30; Bozeman MT $27-30 (jobs.arena.run, Landslide Political, JobTarget)
paidCanvasserHourly.note: Scale by local wage level; floor is the local minimum wage

canvassing.use: Checks on totals only; never decides an individual's choice

doorsPerCanvasserHour.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019) (canvassers typically reach 6-8 contacts/hour at ~25-30% contact rate); industry field-program norms
doorsPerCanvasserHour.note: Lower in rural areas (driving between doors), higher in dense apartments

contactRate.definition: share of targeted doors where a target voter answers and talks
contactRate.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019); Green, McGrath & Aronow (2013), 'Field Experiments and the Study of Voter Turnout', J. Elections, Public Opinion & Parties 23(1):27-48

contactsPerHour.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019)

turnoutEffectsVotesPerContact.note: Approximate 'one additional vote per N contacts' from the GOTV meta-analyses; nonpartisan GOTV in low/mid-salience elections; effects smaller in presidential years

doorToDoor.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019); Green, McGrath & Aronow 2013

volunteerPhone.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019)

commercialPhoneLive.note: well-scripted/coached commercial calls closer to 1 per 35-50
commercialPhoneLive.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019)

robocall.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019)

directMailNonpartisan.note: partisan advocacy mail ~0 turnout effect; social-pressure mail much larger (Gerber, Green & Larimer 2008 APSR: +8.1 pts for 'Neighbors' mailer)
directMailNonpartisan.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019); Gerber, Green & Larimer (2008), APSR 102(1):33-48

television.note: GOTV TV ~0.5 pct-point turnout lift in heavily treated markets (Green & Vavreck 2008; Panagopoulos & Green 2008 radio); persuasive TV effects ~5 pts per 1,000 GRPs that decay within about a week (Gerber, Gimpel, Green & Shaw 2011 APSR 105(1):135-150)

costPerVoteUSD.source: Green, Donald P. & Alan S. Gerber, Get Out the Vote: How to Increase Voter Turnout, 4th ed. (Brookings, 2019) summary table as reproduced in a University of Kentucky MPA thesis (edition not confirmed)

generalElection.note: Average persuasive effect of campaign contact and ads in general elections is about zero

primariesAndBallotMeasures.note: Detectable effects, roughly 1-2 pct points, when contact is early or the race is low-information

persuasionEffects.source: Kalla, Joshua L. & David E. Broockman (2018), 'The Minimal Persuasive Effects of Campaign Contact in General Elections: Evidence from 49 Field Experiments', APSR 112(1):148-166
